source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Sections 2.4--2.8 and 3 as rendered on arXiv
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies ITE prediction intervals under partially identified potential-outcome couplings, extends discussion to ordinal outcomes, and states sharp ITE pmf bounds.
The paper assumes identified potential-outcome marginals without identified dependence, develops sharp treatment-effect distribution bounds, and studies their inference.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corroborating the cited JEBS article; journal text unavailable in this review
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work targets ordinal-outcome probabilities of benefit and strict benefit and gives sharp fixed-marginal bounds for those scalar estimands.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv preprint corroborating the cited Statistics & Probability Letters article; journal text unavailable in this review
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives finite Strassen coupling conditions and a deficiency form from weighted Hall-style conditions for a fixed relation.
The paper constructs minimum-average-volume confidence regions for a multinomial/simplex parameter.
The paper constructs a pointwise-consistent confidence interval for the partially identified fraction who benefit with ordinal or binary outcomes in randomized trials.
Under its stated Gaussian-limit and support assumptions, full differentiability is necessary and sufficient for standard-bootstrap consistency for directionally differentiable functionals.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119, 2024
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper reduces discrete causal questions to polynomial programs and uses dual relaxation plus spatial branch-and-bound to compute sharp bounds.
The paper gives a dynamic-programming procedure with near-optimal volume among unions of k intervals under ordinary conformal prediction coverage.
The cited randomized severe-Covid trial uses day-14 clinical status on a seven-point ordinal scale.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a short proposition comparing the new arbitrary-set oracle directly to the exact interval oracle in ZhangRichardson2025, including the precise nesting relation and the L=2 reduction; this would make the strict extension auditable from one displayed comparator chain.
Develop the equality-regime OEQ into an inverse theorem that states necessary marginal-mass and additive-structure conditions, rather than only asking whether other extremizers exist.

Add a finite-sample cardinality-selection corollary giving an explicit sample-size condition under which the certified selector has the population-optimal cardinality, complementing exact-set recovery away from ties.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the field-tier kernel centered on the sharp interval-price theorem and retain selector recovery as a conditional fixed-margin result.
